sheet-1-1.description: The upper left of Sheet 1, the title sheet of the atlas, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north slightly left of straight up. It covers the edge of Franklin south of the business district: Cummins Street running in from the left at the top, High Street crossing the middle of the part diagonally, and Rutherford Avenue running down from the top to merge with the State Highway along the right side, where a heavy line separates the map from the key map, the location map and the index of the title sheet. Along Cummins Street and Rutherford Avenue are two-storey dwellings with sheds and auto houses, numbered company houses (7-1 to 7-9) and a few stores; a vacant church lit by electricity and heated by stoves stands on the east side of Rutherford Avenue at High Street, and an automobile repair garage and a row of small dwellings line its lower stretch. The lower left is occupied by the site of The New Jersey Zinc Co. Mill No. 1, marked as not in operation, with only scattered vacant buildings and the curving bed of a former track left. A railroad and an eight-inch water pipe run diagonally across the part between Cummins Street and Rutherford Avenue. The bottom of the part is largely blank: a dimension line on the right states that the ground between here and the vocational school drawn below is about 1140 feet and not drawn to scale.
notes: The State Highway is today NJ 23; Rutherford Avenue merges with it at Mitchell Avenue.
The part is separated from part 2 (the Franklin Vocational School) by about 1140 ft that are not drawn to scale, so the two are placed separately.

Placed from two hand-picked points (High Street / Rutherford Avenue and the merge of Rutherford Avenue with the State Highway) as a helmert fit; the detector paired a line south of High Street and was not used.

Title sheet. Left of the heavy line: two map parts at 100 ft (part 1: Cummins, High, Rutherford Av., State Highway; part 2: Franklin Vocational School and School St., about 1140 ft south of part 1, marked not to scale). Right of the line: key map (700 ft), location map, index, notes: not georeferenced.

sheet-1-2.description: The lower left of Sheet 1, the title sheet of the atlas, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. It shows the Franklin Vocational School and its grounds south of the town centre, about 1140 feet south of the streets drawn at the top of the sheet; the gap between them is marked on the sheet as not to scale. Rutherford Avenue, with the State Highway alongside it, runs down the right side of the part, and School Street leaves it to the west, continuing as an unpaved drive past the school. The school is a large brick building of one and two storeys with a laboratory wing, an auditorium and a fireproof section marked as built in 1916; it is heated by steam, lit by electricity and carries chemical extinguishers, with a fire hose and a standpipe in the building and hydrants and a tool house in the grounds. Eight-inch water pipes run past the school on the north and west sides. Along a lane south of School Street are the teachers' dwellings, a row of two-storey frame houses with auto houses, and a few more dwellings and outbuildings face Rutherford Avenue. The rest of the part, including a large north arrow and the sheet's scale bar, is open ground.
notes: School Street is today Washington Avenue; Rutherford Avenue here is today NJ 23.
The part is about 1140 ft south of part 1, a distance the sheet marks as not to scale, so it is placed on its own.
Anchored on one hand-picked point (School Street / Rutherford Avenue) with the atlas scale and north from the sheet's arrow; low confidence.

Title sheet. Left of the heavy line: two map parts at 100 ft (part 1: Cummins, High, Rutherford Av., State Highway; part 2: Franklin Vocational School and School St., about 1140 ft south of part 1, marked not to scale). Right of the line: key map (700 ft), location map, index, notes: not georeferenced.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 shows the commercial centre of Franklin, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points toward the left edge of the sheet. Main Street, the State Highway, enters from the upper left and bends across the lower half of the sheet, with Parker Street branching from it at the Colonial Inn and running up to a fork where it meets High Street. Junction Street leaves Main near the bottom and meets High Street on the right, enclosing the blocks numbered 7 and 8. Nestor Street and Cummins Street appear along the upper left. The Main Street frontage carries the Colonial Inn, Snyder's Hotel, a barber shop, the Neighborhood House with steam heat and electric light, a bake house with ovens, a drug store and a row of stores with a gas pump at the lower right, most of them in the numbered company house lots. Dwellings with sheds and auto houses line High Street and the north side of Nestor Street. The Borough Hall, in pink, stands near the right edge beside the Lehigh and Hudson River Railroad, which runs diagonally down the right side with a long double line of track. A strip along the right edge is lettered as Shuster Park. The sheet also shows a mine shaft and an open pit of the New Jersey Zinc Company at the lower right, a number of six-inch and five-inch water pipes with hydrants, and a dotted line marking the boundary of the lots held by the company. Parts of the margin are blank and carry the numbers of adjoining sheets (3, 4, 5, 6).
notes: Main Street is the old State Highway, today NJ 23.
The sheet is turned so that north points to the left; its fitted rotation differs by about 160 degrees from sheet 3, which joins it at the bottom.
High Street, Parker Street and Junction Street keep their names in OpenStreetMap; the sheet fits at 7.9 px/ft with the Main Street and High Street junctions.
Franklin business district (Main, Parker, High, Junction, Nestor, Cummins), 50 ft, north to the left. 4 detected points.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the New Jersey Zinc Company's Mill No. 2, the zinc mine and ore crushing and separating plant on the east side of Franklin, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the right. The mill buildings fill the middle of the sheet: Separator No. 4, the engine and dynamo room, the crusher house, ore bins, the dust houses and Separator No. 1 at the right, with a machine shop, carpenter shop, supply house, palmer shaft hoist house, change house and lockers, blacksmith shop and a mine office along the left and lower parts. A frame of heavy railroad lines crosses the top and right: the Lehigh and Hudson River Railroad and the New York, Susquehanna and Western Railroad with their sidings, a coal pile and a freight depot. A row of company dwellings numbered 9-45 to 5-4 faces Susquehanna Street along the top edge, north of the railroad. At the bottom Main Street runs across with the employees' garage, a garage, the fire department, first aid rooms and a store, with Parker Street entering from the south and Junction Street at the lower left. Mill Street and Sterling Street appear at the lower right. A block of notes on the watch service, sprinklers and water supply of the mill is printed at the lower right, and the sheet is stamped by the Princeton map division. Hydrants, six-inch and four-inch water pipes, a standpipe and a tank are marked. The blocks at the upper left, bottom and right are blank paper belonging to sheets 2, 4 and 6.
notes: The sheet is placed from only three junction points (Main Street and Parker Street, Main Street and Junction Street, and Mill Street and Sterling Street); the Mill Street and Sterling Street point was hand-picked.
The streets of the mill area are private works and are not in OpenStreetMap.
New Jersey Zinc Co. Mill No. 2 and rail yards (L&HR, NYS&W), Main, Junction, Parker, Mill, Sterling, Susquehanna; 50 ft. Only 3 junctions (one hand-picked): exact fit.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the centre of Franklin north-west of the business district, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Main Street (the State Highway) crosses the lower half of the sheet from Mill Street on the left to Hudson Street on the right, with Sterling Street parallel above it and Nestor Street along the bottom; Larue Street and Cummins Street run down from Main and Nestor at the lower left. The blocks between Sterling and Main hold a row of numbered company dwellings (6-28 to 6-59) along Sterling, with stores, a drug store, a meat market, a furniture and fruit store, an automobile repair garage of concrete block and a concrete-block store building along the Main Street frontage. South of Main the lots carry two-storey dwellings with sheds and auto houses, and a terrace of small dwellings faces Larue Street. The upper half of the sheet is New Jersey Zinc Company land: the tracks of the Lehigh and Hudson River and the New York, Susquehanna and Western railroads cross the top, with a pipe shop, a tool house, fuel oil tanks, an oil pump house, a large circular reclaimed water tank for manufacturing purposes, track scales, an underground store of explosives and a tailings dump; a railroad siding with scales runs along the north side of Sterling Street. The sheet refers to Sheet 3 for the notes on the zinc works. Six-inch water pipes run along Main, Hudson and Larue streets, with hydrants marked at several corners.
notes: Main Street is the old State Highway, today NJ 23 through Franklin.
Sterling and Hudson are lettered without a suffix; today Sterling Street and Hudson Street.
The junctions of Sterling Street with Mill and Hudson streets were hand-picked: Sterling's far side is cut by the sheet edge.
Pilot. Main St. between Mill and Hudson, Sterling, Larue, Nestor, Cummins; zinc company yard at top. North to the upper right.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the north-eastern part of Franklin, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Main Street and Sterling Street run across the upper left between Hudson Street and Lehigh Street, lined with company dwellings numbered in the 2- and 6- series. Rutherford Avenue, a long diagonal, crosses the middle from the lower left to the upper right, with Spry Street, Mabie Street and McCann Street branching from it. The blocks numbered 22, 24, 25 and 38 hold detached dwellings, a garage building in blue and the Wet Wash laundry. A brook with a branch of the railroad follows a curve down the upper right, and the State Highway, marked under construction, crosses the sheet from the lower left to the right, with a double line of railroad track beside it. The lower half is a grid of small lots between Mabie Street, Butler Street, Moscow Street, North Street, Front Street and South Street, nearly all of them dwellings. A heavy black boundary line runs across the left side and down the middle, separating the blocks west of it numbered 42 to 47, where Rutherford Avenue, Warren Street and Master Street serve more dwellings and a stretch of State Highway under construction. Green Street appears at the upper right with a feed and lumber yard of Reeve Harden Co. and again at the lower left. The H. I. Siegel clothing manufacturing building stands at the left edge. A scale bar of 100 feet is printed at the bottom.
notes: Rutherford Avenue is Rutherford Avenue north of Mitchell Avenue and NJ 23 south of it in OpenStreetMap; the drawn State Highway under construction is today's NJ 23.
A watercourse in the upper right is lettered Brook, without a fuller name.
The drawn scale is 100 feet to an inch; the fit gives 3.90 px/ft.
The detector rejected the junction of McCann Street and Rutherford Avenue (12.7 m from the fit); the blocks at the lower left (42 to 47) have no control points of their own.

North-east Franklin (Rutherford Av., Main, Hudson, Lehigh, Mabie, McCann, Butler, Green, Master), 100 ft, one part (the heavy line is a boundary). McCann / Rutherford rejected (12.7 m); blocks 42-47 at the lower left have no control of their own.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 shows the west side of Franklin along the Wallkill River, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the top, tilted slightly left. The river winds across the upper left and appears again at the bottom. Fowler Street runs down the left side as a row of dwellings between the railroad and Wampus Road, and Church Street curves across the lower left past the First Presbyterian Church and the Roman Catholic Church of the Immaculate Conception with its parish house, ending near Oak Street and the plant of Zester and Williams Inc., broad silk manufacturers, with a synagogue beside it. Main Street, the State Highway, runs diagonally from the upper right to the middle, where the Superintendent's Residence of the New Jersey Zinc Company stands among the company's offices, a laboratory, a sawmill and storage, all inside a dotted boundary. Private roads and four-inch and six-inch water pipes cross the company land. At the top right Main Street carries the Franklin Theatre, a bank, a post office and several stores near High Street, where the Lehigh and Hudson River Railroad runs beside a mine. The passenger depot of the New York, Susquehanna and Western is at the top left, with Susquehanna Street and Junction Street at the head of the sheet, and a long block of lots along Lackawanna at the lower left. Blocks of vacant lots and mining land carry the numbers 27 to 31.
notes: Placed from one hand-picked junction (High Street and Main Street) at the atlas scale and the rotation given by it and the Church Street and Main Street junction, whose modern node lies about 30 m from the drawn one; the modern street pattern differs from the 1928 pattern on the left side of the sheet, so the placement is weak.
Wampus Road, Private Road and Public Road are not in OpenStreetMap under those names.
The drawn scale is 100 feet to an inch.

West Franklin along the Wallkill (Main, High, Church, Fowler, Junction, Wampus Rd., Lackawanna), 100 ft. Old street pattern differs from today's; the detector found nothing. Anchored on High St. / Main St. (hand-picked) at the atlas scale (3.94 px/ft) and the rotation of the two hand picks; Church / Main hand pick left out (its modern node about 30 m from the drawn junction, 7 percent scale error).

sheet-7-1.description: The upper part of Sheet 7, above a heavy dividing line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that the edge it shares with Sheet 8 is at the top. It shows the south-western part of Franklin around the passenger station of the New York, Susquehanna and Western Railroad. The Wallkill River winds across the upper left, crossed by Church Street on a bridge at the left edge; Church Street runs from there to Franklin Avenue, which climbs to the top of the sheet past The New Jersey Zinc Co. water works filter plant, with covered filter beds and a concrete pump house with electric rotary pumps, beside the outlet of Franklin Pond. Cork Hill Road leaves Franklin Avenue to the right. Railroad Avenue curves from Church Street down to the tracks, where the N.Y.S. & W. R.R. passenger depot and scales stand, and Maple Road runs down to the lower right from the crossing, with lots and scattered dwellings on both sides. Along Church Street are the Washington Hotel, a garage with a gasoline tank, a milk depot near the bridge, stores and dwellings. A further stretch of Church Street continues past the railroad at the right. Eight-inch and six-inch water pipes cross the upper part of the sheet to the filter plant, and the dash-dot match line lettered C and D at the top marks the join with Sheet 8.
notes: The 1928 street pattern here differs from today's: the modern Church Street, Cork Hill Road and Dixon Road follow parts of the drawn Franklin Avenue, Maple Road and Railroad Avenue, and junctions on the modern lines disagreed by 14 to 20 m, so they were not used.
Placed from three points carried from Sheet 8 along the shared match line C-D: low confidence away from the top of the sheet.
The lower part of the sheet (Cork Hill Road, the New Jersey Calcite Co. limestone quarries) is not placed.

Two parts separated by a heavy line, north to the right: part 1 Church St./Franklin Av./Railroad Av./Maple Rd. at the NYS&W passenger depot; part 2 Cork Hill Rd. with cement block houses and New Jersey Calcite Co. limestone quarries. Old road pattern differs from today's (Dixon Road etc.). Part 1 placed from three points carried from sheet 8 (the dash-dot match line C-D); its modern junctions (Church / Cork Hill, Church / Dixon) disagreed by 14 to 20 m and were left out. Part 2 not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: lower part below the heavy line: Cork Hill Rd., Church St. bridge over the N.Y.S.&W. R.R., cement block houses, New Jersey Calcite Co. limestone quarries (no junction identified with confidence; the 1928 roads south of the town differ from today's; needs identification of the Church St. / Cork Hill Rd. junction on modern data, or parcel corners (step 6b)).

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers the southern edge of Franklin between Franklin Pond and the State Highway, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Franklin Avenue runs up the left side of the sheet along the east shore of Franklin Pond, from its junction with Rutherford Avenue at the lower left to the edge of Sheet 7 at the top; Rutherford Avenue crosses the bottom of the sheet. Most of the ground is open company land crossed by dashed private roads. The largest building is the New Jersey Zinc Co's Hospital, of brick and frame, lit by electricity and steam heated, with a doctor's house and a 10,000-gallon water tank near it; a private road leads to it from Franklin Avenue. To the east stands The Brick Row, a terrace of two-storey brick company dwellings, with further company houses and outbuildings near the roads marked as arbitrarily named, Byrom Road at the top and Seneca Road along the right side. An old limestone quarry is outlined at the top centre. Scattered dwellings, a store with gasoline tanks and an auto repair shop stand along Franklin Avenue, and a row of dwellings with auto houses lines the north side of Rutherford Avenue. A six-inch water pipe runs from the hospital to The Brick Row and a two-inch pipe along it.
notes: Byrom Road and Seneca Road are marked as arbitrary names on the sheet and in the index.
The private road to the hospital and the private road east of it are today Hospital Road and Kane Street; Rutherford Avenue here is today South Rutherford Avenue, bypassed by NJ 23.
The 1928 Franklin Avenue curved into Rutherford Avenue along today's Old Franklin Avenue; the modern Franklin Avenue runs straight on to NJ 23.
Placed from three hand-picked points (an exact first-order fit); the detector found nothing on the curved and dashed roads.
South Franklin: Franklin Av. along Franklin Pond, Rutherford Av., New Jersey Zinc Co's Hospital, The Brick Row, private and arbitrary roads. North to the upper right.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 shows Ogdensburg, about three miles south of the Franklin post office, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north pointing to the right. The centre of the sheet is The New Jersey Zinc Co. Sterling Hill Plant, a zinc mine and ore crushing, washing and separating plant: a large mill building of hollow tile and steel with dust bins and a balcony, a crusher, a machine shop, a transformer house, ore bins of corrugated iron on steel, a locomotive house, a diamond drill core house, a supply house, an office and car sheds, with a railroad trestle and sidings crossing the works and a 50,000-gallon water tank on the hill above. The outline of the Sterling Hill Mine workings is drawn above the plant. A note gives the plant's fire protection, from night watchman and hydrants to hose houses. Public Road runs below the works, Franklin Road (marked arbitrary) leaves it to the right, and Wild Cat Road runs along the right side. At the left are company dwellings on Avenue A and Avenue B, with a neighborhood house and bowling alleys. Below, the Wallkill River crosses the sheet; south of it Lilac runs to the lower left with a row of brick and frame dwellings, and at the lower right Centre and Passaic Avenue cross a block of lots with scattered houses; a note says it is about 500 feet from there to Sheet 10. At the upper right a row of company houses lines Wausau, a road also marked arbitrary. The New York, Susquehanna and Western Railroad runs along the lower right edge.
notes: Public Road is today Plant Street; Franklin Road is today Cork Hill Road; Wild Cat Road at the right is today Passaic Avenue; Lilac is today Bridge Street; Centre is today Center Street.
Franklin Road and Wausau are marked as arbitrary names on the sheet.

Placed from two detected junctions (Avenue A / Avenue B and Avenue B / Public Road) and one hand-picked junction (Public Road / Wild Cat Road / Franklin Road): an exact fit through three points, low confidence away from them, especially south of the river.
Ogdensburg: New Jersey Zinc Co. Sterling Hill Plant, Avenue A and B, Public Rd., Wild Cat Rd., Lilac, Centre, Passaic Av., Wausau. North to the right.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 is the village of Ogdensburg, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the top. A title note near the top reads Ogdensburg, located 3 miles south of the post office, population 1100, with a description of the village water works and fire department. Sparta Road runs across the middle of the sheet, with the post office, a hotel, a bakery, stores and two public schools along it; Passaic Avenue climbs to the north between the village blocks and a diagonal Railroad Avenue runs up to the New York, Susquehanna and Western tracks at the upper right, where the lumber yard and coal yard of W. C. Chambers stand. Church Street branches from Passaic Avenue, with a church and a Presbyterian church close by. South of Sparta Road a grid of streets, Highland Avenue, Edison Road, Spring Street, Clark Street and High Street, bounds blocks numbered 57 to 64 containing the borough hall and fire department, a small pink building and scattered dwellings. Edison Road curves to the lower left past Street No. 1, and Fairview Avenue and an unnamed street lie at the lower left. Hydrants are marked at the corners, with six-inch water pipes along most of the streets. The upper left is blank paper, and sheet 9 is noted as about 500 feet to the north.
notes: Sparta Road is Main Street in OpenStreetMap, and Railroad Avenue is today's Kennedy Avenue.
Highland Avenue and Main Street (14.6 m) and Kennedy Avenue and Main Street (7.3 m) were rejected by the detector as displaced.
A street at the lower left is lettered Not Named.
The drawn scale is 100 feet to an inch.
Ogdensburg village (Sparta Rd. = Main Street, Passaic Av., Highland Av., Railroad Av. = Kennedy Avenue, Edison Rd.), 100 ft, north up. Highland / Main and Kennedy / Main rejected as displaced.
